event: Israeli airstrikes in eastern and southern Lebanon resulted in at least 31 deaths and dozens of injuries, while both Hezbollah and Israel reported increased ground operations and cross-border attacks despite an existing ceasefire agreement.

verified_facts.statement: Israeli airstrikes occurred in eastern and southern Lebanon resulting in at least 31 deaths and dozens of injuries
verified_facts.source_url: https://www.bbc.com/news or https://www.aljazeera.com (news archives from relevant dates)
verified_facts.note: Casualty figures from this event are reported across international news sources; exact death toll varies slightly by source and timing of reporting

verified_facts.statement: A ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hezbollah was in place during the period of these airstrikes
verified_facts.note: Multiple ceasefire agreements were announced; this fact refers to the existence of at least one formal agreement during the reported airstrike period

verified_facts.statement: Both Israeli and Hezbollah forces reported military operations and cross-border attacks during the ceasefire period
verified_facts.source_url: IDF statements, Hezbollah statements, news reports
verified_facts.note: Both sides publicly acknowledged continued military activity; specific operation details vary by source

verified_facts.statement: Over one million people were displaced from Lebanon during the broader conflict
verified_facts.note: UN humanitarian agencies documented displacement figures; this is a cumulative figure from the broader 2024 conflict, not solely from this airstrike event

verified_facts.statement: Israeli troops maintained a presence in Lebanese territory during this period
verified_facts.source_url: IDF statements, Lebanese government statements, news reports
verified_facts.note: Both Israeli and Lebanese sources acknowledged Israeli military presence; characterization as 'occupation' or 'security zones' is contested

verified_facts.statement: Lebanese army officers were killed in Israeli strikes
verified_facts.note: Documented in multiple reports; exact numbers and circumstances vary by source

verified_facts.statement: Hezbollah was not a signatory to the ceasefire agreement
verified_facts.source_url: U.S. State Department, UN statements, news reports
verified_facts.note: Widely reported that Hezbollah did not formally sign the ceasefire; Iran's role in Hezbollah decision-making is separately contested

verified_facts.statement: The U.S. attempted to broker and enforce ceasefire agreements involving Israel and Lebanese/Hezbollah forces
verified_facts.source_url: U.S. State Department statements, news reports
verified_facts.note: U.S. diplomatic engagement is documented; the effectiveness and nature of pressure applied is contested

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Trump made an expletive-laden phone call to Netanyahu pressuring him to stop strikes on Beirut
unverified_shared_claims.note: Reported in some news outlets but not independently verified by primary record; details of private conversations are inherently difficult to confirm

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Hezbollah is actively rebuilding its military arsenal in violation of the ceasefire
unverified_shared_claims.note: Israeli and U.S. officials claim this; Hezbollah and Lebanese sources dispute or deny; no independent verification mechanism exists

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Hezbollah rejected multiple U.S.-brokered ceasefire proposals
unverified_shared_claims.note: Claimed by U.S. and Israeli sources; Hezbollah's stated reasons and the exact sequence of proposals are contested

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Iran has explicitly linked Lebanon ceasefire to broader U.S.-Iran negotiations
unverified_shared_claims.note: Reported in news sources citing Iranian statements; the precise nature and binding force of this linkage is unclear

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Israeli strikes constitute systematic war crimes under international law
unverified_shared_claims.note: Legal characterization disputed; no international court has made this determination; requires investigation and adjudication

points_of_disagreement: Whether Israeli airstrikes are proportionate responses to Hezbollah attacks or violations of international law and the ceasefire
Whether Hezbollah or Israel bears primary responsibility for ceasefire violations
Whether Israeli military presence in Lebanon constitutes 'occupation' or legitimate 'security zones'
Whether Hezbollah's exclusion from negotiations is a structural flaw or appropriate given its designation as a terrorist organization by some states
Whether the primary driver of continued violence is Hezbollah's refusal to withdraw/disarm or Israel's refusal to cease operations
Whether U.S. pressure on Israel is sufficient, excessive, or strategically incoherent
Whether Iran's role is as a controlling force over Hezbollah or as a legitimate stakeholder in regional de-escalation
Whether the conflict should be analyzed as a bilateral Israel-Hezbollah dispute or as part of a broader Iran-Israel-U.S. confrontation
Whether civilian casualties are incidental to legitimate military operations or evidence of indiscriminate targeting
Whether Lebanese sovereignty is being violated by Israeli operations or protected by Israeli counter-terrorism actions
shared_foundation.summary: All framings accept that Israeli airstrikes killed at least 31 people in Lebanon during a ceasefire period, that both Israeli and Hezbollah forces conducted military operations despite the agreement, that over one million were displaced, and that Hezbollah was not a formal signatory to ceasefire terms. The disagreements concern causation (who violated first and why), legal characterization (proportionality, war crimes, sovereignty), and strategic diagnosis (whether the conflict is bilateral, Iranian-proxy, or a failed diplomatic architecture).

framings.name: International Law & War Crimes Accountability
framings.question: Do Israel's continued strikes on Lebanon despite an active ceasefire constitute violations of international humanitarian law, and who should be held accountable?
framings.key_claim: Israel's near-daily airstrikes on Lebanese territory after the ceasefire agreement systematically violate international law, causing documented civilian casualties and infrastructure destruction that amount to war crimes.
framings.description: This framing treats the strikes primarily as a legal and human rights matter, centering on IHL obligations, the prohibition on destruction of civilian property, and the absence of accountability for documented violations. It draws heavily on UN mechanisms and NGO satellite analysis.
framings.emphasizes: Verified civilian death counts, destruction of civilian infrastructure, IHL prohibitions, calls for independent investigations, UN documentation, and the asymmetry between Israeli and Hezbollah violations.
framings.downplays: Israel's stated security rationale (Hezbollah military buildup, ongoing rocket fire), the complexity of dual-use targeting, and Hezbollah's own ceasefire violations.
sample_headlines: UN experts warn against continued violations of ceasefire in Lebanon and urge protection of civilians (OHCHR, Oct 2025)
Lebanon: Israel systematic attacks and killings threaten peace efforts, UN expert warns (OHCHR, Nov 2025)
Israel's extensive destruction of Southern Lebanon (Amnesty International, Aug 2025)

carriers.name: OHCHR / UN Special Rapporteurs
carriers.excerpt: "Despite the ceasefire, Israel continues to strike Lebanese territory almost daily"
carriers.role_evidence: UN Special Rapporteurs produced the earliest systematic legal framing, citing verified civilian casualties and calling for accountability investigations.

carriers.name: Amnesty International
carriers.excerpt: "Such destruction should be investigated as a war crime wherever it was carried out intentionally or recklessly"
carriers.role_evidence: Amnesty's satellite-imagery-backed research on 10,000+ destroyed structures in southern Lebanon gave empirical grounding to the war-crimes framing.

carriers.name: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
carriers.excerpt: "For a year now, airstrikes and shelling have persisted despite the ceasefire agreement. This is not what a ceasefire looks like"
carriers.role_evidence: Widely cited NRC one-year ceasefire report aggregated UNIFIL violation counts (7,500+ airspace violations) and humanitarian data, amplifying the accountability framing broadly.

carriers.name: UN Special Rapporteur Morris Tidball-Binz
carriers.excerpt: "These repeated attacks on civilians and civilian objects are war crimes and a violation of the UN Charter"
carriers.role_evidence: Issued formal UN declaration labeling strikes 'war crimes,' representing the UN Human Rights Council's institutional adoption of the accountability framing.

carriers.name: Israel Ministry of Foreign Affairs / IDF Spokesperson
carriers.excerpt: Israel says it is striking terror operatives plotting attacks against troops and Israeli communities.
carriers.role_evidence: Israeli officials consistently reject the war-crimes framing, asserting strikes are lawful self-defense against active Hezbollah military targets.

framings.name: Israeli Self-Defense & Counter-Terrorism
framings.question: Is Israel exercising a legitimate right to self-defense against an active terrorist threat that is rebuilding military capabilities and firing into Israeli territory?
framings.key_claim: Every Israeli strike is a proportionate response to Hezbollah's ongoing rocket, drone, and missile attacks on northern Israeli communities, and to the group's documented violations of the ceasefire by rebuilding its arsenal.
framings.description: This framing positions Israel as the reactive party, emphasizing Hezbollah's ceasefire violations (military rebuilding, cross-border fire), ongoing threat to Israeli civilians, and Israel's sovereign right to eliminate active threats. It is the dominant framing in Israeli official communications and pro-Israel Western commentary.
framings.emphasizes: Hezbollah's rocket and drone attacks, IDF soldier casualties, Iranian backing of Hezbollah, Hezbollah's military infrastructure rebuild, northern Israel civilian displacement.
framings.downplays: The casualty asymmetry, civilian deaths from Israeli strikes, international law constraints on targeting, and the pattern of near-daily strikes pre-dating any specific Hezbollah provocation.
sample_headlines: Soldier killed in anti-tank missile attack as Hezbollah rejects Lebanon ceasefire proposal (Times of Israel, Jun 2026)
Netanyahu: 'We will not allow firing at our territory or our communities, and we will act accordingly' (NPR/Netanyahu statement, Jun 2026)
IDF: Hezbollah violated ceasefire by rebuilding militant infrastructure and weapons arsenal (Wikipedia / IDF statements)

carriers.name: Office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu
carriers.excerpt: "We are striking them very hard, and we know that Hezbollah is on the run. We will not allow firing at our territory"
carriers.role_evidence: Netanyahu's office directly framed strikes as retaliatory self-defense responses to Hezbollah provocations in official statements and X posts.

carriers.name: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz
carriers.excerpt: "Israel categorically rejects Iran's threats" and will continue operating against Hezbollah in Lebanon.
carriers.role_evidence: Katz's repeated statements maintaining ongoing operations constitute formal institutional adoption of the self-defense framing.

carriers.name: Times of Israel
carriers.excerpt: "An IDF officer was killed in a Hezbollah anti-tank guided missile attack in southern Lebanon"
carriers.role_evidence: The Times of Israel consistently leads with Hezbollah attacks on Israeli forces, centering Israeli casualties and the self-defense frame for English-language audiences.

carriers.name: Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD)
carriers.excerpt: "A new or partial ceasefire could give Hezbollah a morale boost as it seeks to regroup"
carriers.role_evidence: FDD analysis advanced a variant of the self-defense framing that also argued restraint is counterproductive, amplifying it in US hawkish policy circles.

carriers.name: U.S. State Department / U.S. Officials (via Axios)
carriers.excerpt: "The United States supports Israel's right to self-defense and stands with the legitimate Government of Lebanon"
carriers.role_evidence: U.S. officials explicitly endorsed Israel's right to self-defense framing while also calling on Hezbollah to halt fire, lending it institutional backing.

framings.name: Humanitarian / Human Cost
framings.question: Who is being killed, displaced, and dispossessed, and what is the lived reality on the ground for Lebanese civilians caught between the belligerents?
framings.key_claim: Lebanese civilians—including women, children, paramedics, and army officers—are bearing the catastrophic human cost of a conflict that has killed thousands, displaced over one million people, and shattered infrastructure, with no end in sight.
framings.description: This framing centers the scale of human suffering, foregrounding victim identities, displacement figures, psychological toll, and destruction of civilian livelihoods. It is used by humanitarian NGOs, health ministries, and human-interest journalism, and is not inherently partisan.
framings.emphasizes: Death counts, displacement figures, child casualties, destruction of homes and hospitals, fear and psychological trauma, blocked returns of displaced persons.
framings.downplays: The military-strategic logic of the strikes, Hezbollah's role in initiating cycles of violence, and Israeli civilian suffering from Hezbollah rockets.

'For a year now, airstrikes have persisted. This is not what a ceasefire looks like' (NRC Country Director, Nov 2025)
Israeli airstrike on Ein el-Hilweh refugee camp kills 13, including 8 children (OHCHR, Nov 2025)

carriers.name: Lebanese Ministry of Public Health
carriers.excerpt: "cumulative toll from Israeli attacks between March 2 and June 9 had reached 3,666 dead and 11,321 injured"
carriers.role_evidence: Lebanon's health ministry produces the primary casualty counts that anchor all humanitarian framing globally.

carriers.name: NPR (Leila Fadel / Greg Myre dispatches)
carriers.excerpt: "The south has been hit hard, with dozens of villages flattened, so many dead"
carriers.role_evidence: NPR's on-the-ground reporting consistently amplified the human cost framing for a broad U.S. public audience.

carriers.name: UNICEF Lebanon
carriers.excerpt: UNICEF Lebanon reported that more than 13 children had been killed and 146 injured since the ceasefire.
carriers.role_evidence: UNICEF's child-specific casualty data is a key early amplifier of the human cost framing, especially in international media.

carriers.name: Xinhua (English-language state wire)
carriers.excerpt: "months of hostilities have also reshaped transportation routes, civilian movement"
carriers.role_evidence: Xinhua's roundup reporting packages the humanitarian toll for broad international distribution, amplifying the human-cost framing globally.

carriers.excerpt: 64,417 people remain internally displaced, primarily from Bint Jbeil, Marjaayoun, and Sour (IOM).
carriers.role_evidence: IOM displacement figures are regularly cited in humanitarian framing but IOM itself does not actively frame the political dimensions of the conflict.

framings.name: Ceasefire Collapse & Diplomatic Failure
framings.question: Why have multiple ceasefire agreements failed to hold, and what does this reveal about the structural inadequacy of the diplomatic framework?
framings.key_claim: Serial ceasefire collapses—with both Israel and Hezbollah violating successive agreements almost immediately—expose a fatally flawed diplomatic architecture that lacks enforcement mechanisms and excludes the primary belligerent (Hezbollah) from negotiations.
framings.description: This framing treats the ceasefire failures as a lens on diplomacy's limits: the gap between paper agreements and ground realities, Hezbollah's non-signatory status, and Israeli insistence on retaining the right to strike 'threats.' It is used by analytical journalism and foreign-policy think tanks across the spectrum.
framings.emphasizes: The sequence of broken ceasefires since Nov 2024, Hezbollah's exclusion from negotiations, Israel's continued operations despite deals, the structural role of Iran, and the US-Israel tensions over Lebanon strategy.
framings.downplays: The human cost angle, the legal accountability angle, and ideological motivations of the parties.

Israel Risks Another 'Managed' Conflict in Lebanon (FDD, Jun 2026)
Hezbollah rejects Lebanon ceasefire brokered by U.S., Israeli military says it will continue attacks (CBC News, Jun 2026)

carriers.name: Brian Katulis / Middle East Institute (via NPR)
carriers.excerpt: "These ceasefires between Israel and Hezbollah essentially have been quite tenuous, and they've been broken almost on a daily basis"
carriers.role_evidence: Katulis's recurring expert commentary is the clearest articulation of the structural diplomatic-failure framing in English-language coverage.

carriers.name: NPR
carriers.excerpt: "Israel and Lebanon agreed to renew a ceasefire that never really took hold"
carriers.role_evidence: NPR's news framing consistently highlighted the structural fragility of ceasefires, amplifying the diplomatic-failure lens to mass audiences.

carriers.name: CBC News
carriers.excerpt: "Hezbollah rejects Lebanon ceasefire brokered by U.S., Israeli military says it will continue attacks"
carriers.role_evidence: CBC's headline encapsulates the diplomatic-failure framing in a single line, widely shared in North American media ecosystems.

carriers.name: Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD)
carriers.excerpt: "A recent flurry of diplomatic activity suggests Israel is restricted to a managed conflict, echoing previous inconclusive rounds"
carriers.role_evidence: FDD's analysis warned about a structural repeat of prior managed-conflict dynamics, amplifying the diplomatic-failure framing from a pro-Israel strategic lens.

carriers.name: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem (Al-Manar TV)
carriers.excerpt: Qassem called the Washington negotiations "absurd, humiliating and insulting."
carriers.role_evidence: Hezbollah's public rejection of the ceasefire deal—and its insistence on Israeli withdrawal as a precondition—directly challenges the legitimacy of the diplomatic framework.

framings.name: Lebanese Sovereignty & State Integrity
framings.question: How do continuing Israeli strikes and a partial territorial occupation undermine Lebanon's sovereignty, and can a weak Lebanese state assert itself against both Hezbollah and Israeli military presence?
framings.key_claim: Israel's retention of 'security zones,' near-daily strikes, and killing of Lebanese army officers amount to an ongoing occupation that violates Lebanese sovereignty and undermines the Lebanese government's ability to exercise authority over its own territory.
framings.description: This framing foregrounds Lebanon as an injured sovereign state—distinct from Hezbollah—whose government, army, and president are simultaneously condemning both Hezbollah's unauthorized warfare and Israel's occupation. It is prominent in Lebanese state communications, regional press, and some Western coverage.
framings.emphasizes: Israeli troops in Lebanese territory, strikes on Lebanese army officers, Lebanon's president and government statements, the distinction between the Lebanese state and Hezbollah, the demand for full Israeli withdrawal.
framings.downplays: Hezbollah's role in provoking Israeli responses and its long history of operating as a state-within-a-state in Lebanon.

Lebanese President condemns Israel's 'continuing violations' (2026 Lebanon–Israel Ceasefire, Wikipedia)
Israeli forces retain five military outposts in southern Lebanon beyond deadline (AP/Wikipedia, Feb 2025)

carriers.name: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun
carriers.excerpt: "The continued, deliberate, and repeated Israeli aggression against Lebanon, its people and its army only strengthens our resolve"
carriers.role_evidence: President Aoun is the primary originator of the Lebanese sovereignty framing, consistently framing Israeli strikes as attacks on the Lebanese state itself.

carriers.name: Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA)
carriers.excerpt: Israel's attacks aim to thwart efforts "to reach a solution that would restore stability… and lead to the Israeli withdrawal from the occupied Lebanese territories."
carriers.role_evidence: NNA is the official Lebanese state news wire that amplifies Aoun's and the government's sovereignty framing to international outlets.

carriers.name: UN Special Rapporteur / OHCHR (April 2026)
carriers.excerpt: "Since the cessation of hostilities between Lebanon and Israel on 27 November 2024, Israel has repeatedly violated Lebanon's sovereignty"
carriers.role_evidence: OHCHR's institutional adoption of the sovereignty-violation framing gave it authoritative mass amplification in international media.

carriers.name: Brazil / International Community Condemnations
carriers.excerpt: Brazil condemned 8 April 2026 Israeli attacks in Lebanon as a breach of the April 2026 ceasefire, demanding Israel suspend military operations.
carriers.role_evidence: Multiple states formally adopting Lebanon's sovereignty framing at the governmental level, institutionalizing it in international diplomacy.

carriers.name: Israel Defense Ministry / IDF
carriers.excerpt: Israel "categorically rejects" Iran's threats and will continue operations in Lebanon against Hezbollah.
carriers.role_evidence: Israel consistently denies the occupation/sovereignty-violation framing, arguing it targets only Hezbollah military assets and retains the right of self-defense.

framings.name: US-Israel Geopolitical Tension & Alliance Management
framings.question: Is Israel undermining U.S. strategic interests by continuing its Lebanon offensive in defiance of American ceasefire efforts, and what does this reveal about the limits of U.S. influence over Israel?
framings.key_claim: Israel's insistence on continuing Lebanon strikes despite direct White House pressure—including a reportedly expletive-laden Trump phone call—is straining the U.S.-Israel alliance and jeopardizing Trump's Iran deal and regional de-escalation goals.
framings.description: This framing treats Lebanon as a case study in U.S.-Israel alliance management, centering on Trump's frustration with Netanyahu, the tension between Israel's military objectives and U.S. diplomatic goals with Iran, and the limits of American leverage. It appeals to foreign-policy realists across the political spectrum.
framings.emphasizes: Trump-Netanyahu friction, U.S. attempts to restrain Israeli strikes on Beirut, Iran's linkage of Lebanon to U.S.-Iran negotiations, American diplomatic capital expenditure, and the strategic incoherence of U.S. policy.
framings.downplays: The human rights and legal dimensions, and the immediate security threat to Israeli civilians from Hezbollah.

carriers.name: Axios

carriers.role_evidence: Axios's behind-the-scenes sourcing on U.S.-Israel back-channel dynamics was among the first to ground the alliance-tension framing in specific reported details.

carriers.name: CNN
carriers.excerpt: "Trump's phone call with Netanyahu became heated as he pressed Israel to scale back its Lebanon offensive"
carriers.role_evidence: CNN's live coverage of the Trump-Netanyahu confrontation over Lebanon drove the alliance-tension framing to a mass U.S. audience.

carriers.name: NPR
carriers.excerpt: "Trump really seems to want a deal with Iran, so this grabbed his attention"
carriers.role_evidence: NPR's analysis connected the Lebanon strikes directly to the Iran deal calculus, amplifying the strategic-tension framing for a broad public audience.

carriers.name: TIME
carriers.excerpt: "Israel's continued fighting with Hezbollah in Lebanon has also threatened to derail progress towards a U.S.–Iran deal"
carriers.role_evidence: TIME's framing explicitly tied Lebanon to Iran deal diplomacy early, amplifying the geopolitical-tension framing in international political commentary.

carriers.name: Israel's hard-right ministers (Ben-Gvir, Smotrich)
carriers.excerpt: Ben-Gvir called the ceasefire proposal "a serious mistake" and Smotrich argued for intensifying pressure on Hezbollah in Beirut.
carriers.role_evidence: Israel's far-right coalition partners publicly opposed restraint in Lebanon, acting as an internal critic of the framing that U.S. pressure should shape Israeli operations.

framings.name: Hezbollah as Obstructionist Actor
framings.question: Is Hezbollah—by rejecting ceasefires, continuing attacks, and refusing to withdraw—primarily responsible for prolonging civilian suffering in Lebanon and blocking Lebanese state sovereignty?
framings.key_claim: Hezbollah's rejection of multiple U.S.-brokered ceasefires, its refusal to withdraw from southern Lebanon, and its continued rocket and drone attacks are the primary drivers of ongoing violence and the chief obstacle to Lebanese reconstruction and sovereignty.
framings.description: This framing, used by U.S. officials, the Lebanese government itself, and pro-Israel Western media, positions Hezbollah as the spoiler blocking peace—distinct from the Lebanese state and population, and ultimately serving Iranian rather than Lebanese interests.
framings.emphasizes: Hezbollah's ceasefire rejection, its continued firing on Israeli forces, its non-signatory status in negotiations, Iran's control over Hezbollah, and the Lebanese government's own condemnations of the group.
framings.downplays: Israel's continued operations that Hezbollah cites as justification for non-compliance, the structural leverage asymmetry between the parties, and the history of Israeli occupation that underpins Hezbollah's founding rationale.

carriers.name: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun / Prime Minister
carriers.excerpt: Lebanon should not be used by Tehran as a "bargaining chip" in its talks with Washington.
carriers.role_evidence: The Lebanese government's own condemnations of Hezbollah and Iran represent a notable institutional adoption of this framing from an unexpected (non-Israeli, non-U.S.) source.

carriers.role_evidence: NPR's straightforward reporting on Hezbollah's rejection, paired with the Lebanese government's condemnation of Iran, served as mass amplification of this framing.

carriers.name: Times of Israel
carriers.excerpt: "An IDF officer was killed in a Hezbollah anti-tank guided missile attack in southern Lebanon, as the Iran-backed terror group rejected a ceasefire plan"
carriers.role_evidence: Times of Israel's use of 'terror group' language and juxtaposition with IDF casualties consistently frames Hezbollah as the primary obstructionist actor.

carriers.role_evidence: Hezbollah directly contests the 'obstructionist' label, framing its rejection of ceasefires as principled resistance to occupation rather than spoiler behavior.

framings.name: Regional Escalation & Iran Proxy War
framings.question: Are the Lebanon strikes a node in a wider Iran-Israel-US regional proxy conflict, and does continued fighting in Lebanon risk triggering catastrophic regional escalation?
framings.key_claim: Israel's Lebanon strikes are inseparable from the broader Iran-Israel-US confrontation, with Iran's linkage of Lebanon to any wider ceasefire making every airstrike a potential trigger for catastrophic regional escalation involving the Houthis, Iranian ballistic missiles, and U.S. forces.
framings.description: This framing situates the Lebanon strikes within the 2026 Iran war context, emphasizing the interconnectedness of all theaters and the fragility of any partial deal that excludes Lebanon. It is prominent in analytical geopolitical journalism, think-tank commentary, and national security reporting.
framings.emphasizes: Iran's declared linkage of Lebanon to ceasefire with the U.S., Hezbollah as an Iranian proxy, Houthi co-belligerency, U.S. force posture, risk of escalation dominos, and the failure to include Lebanon in the Iran war ceasefire.
framings.downplays: The immediate human cost within Lebanon itself, and the agency of Lebanese actors who are subordinated to the proxy-war narrative.

carriers.role_evidence: CNN's live coverage of the Iran-Israel exchange, linked explicitly to Lebanon operations, drove the escalation-risk framing to a global mass audience.

carriers.name: TIME
carriers.excerpt: "Iran has repeatedly objected to Israel's fighting with Hezbollah and said that a permanent cessation of Israeli attacks across the region is a precondition for any U.S.-Iran deal"
carriers.role_evidence: TIME's analysis explicitly mapped how Lebanon fighting feeds into the Iran nuclear/deal calculus, amplifying the escalation framing in policy-oriented audiences.

carriers.name: Wikipedia / 2026 Lebanon War article (aggregator of sourced events)
carriers.excerpt: Iran called for an end to Israeli attacks in Lebanon as a condition for a wider ceasefire.
carriers.role_evidence: Wikipedia's event aggregation reflects mainstream media consensus framing of Lebanon as part of the wider Iran-proxy-war theater.

carriers.name: Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters (state media)

carriers.role_evidence: Iran's military command directly institutionalizing the escalation-linkage framing in official statements, confirming Lebanon's place in the broader proxy-war frame.

gap_analysis: Missing framings include: (1) Lebanese civilian perspectives on state capacity and protection—why residents remain in conflict zones and their views on Lebanese government effectiveness versus Hezbollah provision of services; (2) Israeli domestic security concerns and civilian casualty narratives from northern Israeli communities under rocket fire; (3) Economic/infrastructure impact framing—damage to Lebanese hospitals, water systems, agriculture, and displacement costs; (4) Ceasefire agreement specifics and enforcement mechanisms—which party violated which terms first, and structural weaknesses in the agreement itself rather than just blame assignment; (5) Regional Sunni Arab state interests (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt) in Lebanon stability versus Iran-aligned actors; (6) Voices from Lebanese political factions outside Hezbollah on how to resolve the conflict.
